data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

extract_result.purpose: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy for identifying, evaluating, and designating information technology (IT) related enterprise initiatives in the form of a recommendation to the USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO). The intent of this DR is to promote the effective and efficient sharing of IT resources across the entire organization to drive down costs and improve customer service. The goal is to create a structured process to address an agency’s or multiple agencies’ desire to have a shared business approach based on a single or multiple business requirements.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy for identifying, evaluating, and designating information technology (IT) related enterprise initiatives in the form of a recommendation to the USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO).
The intent of this DR is to promote the effective and efficient sharing of IT resources across the entire organization to drive down costs and improve customer service.
The goal is to create a structured process to address an agency’s or multiple agencies’ desire to have a shared business approach based on a single or multiple business requirements.
This DR applies to all agencies and staff offices.

Nothing in this DR is intended to supplant the delegation of authorities and responsibilities of the USDA CIO, USDA Chief Financial Officer (CFO), the Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights, and/or the Assistant Secretary for Administration under 7 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 2 or any other authorities otherwise provided by law, Federal regulation, or USDA Departmental Regulation.
cross_references: 7 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 2

policy_statements.source_text: The authority for this DR is derived from 7 CFR 2.89(a)(11)(x), which authorizes the USDA CIO to improve the management and operational effectiveness of information resources.
Enterprise-wide IT initiatives present special opportunities and management challenges for USDA, given its diverse set of missions and component agencies and offices.

For example, the pooling of USDA’s purchasing power across the entire enterprise to purchase a commonly needed product can reduce the total cost of acquisition, but a shared investment in a one-dimensional service may not deliver a useful solution for all agencies and staff offices because of their mission diversity.

The CIO Council (CIOC), established by the USDA CIO and comprised of senior IT representatives from the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) and agencies and staff offices, is uniquely positioned to evaluate potential IT initiatives and designate those with the highest value as enterprise-level initiatives.

The guidance in this DR is established to ensure that IT enterprise initiatives are effectively identified, evaluated, and implemented to accomplish the best possible value for USDA agencies, staff offices, and their customers.
Executive Sponsor: The executive sponsor is a CIOC voting member from one USDA agency or staff office involved in establishing or to benefit from the enterprise initiative.
The executive sponsor shall oversee the analysis and documentation process required for the CIOC evaluation of an enterprise initiative.

Initiative Owner: The initiative owner is an official from one USDA agency or staff office involved in establishing an enterprise initiative and shall be accountable for the establishment and management of an approved enterprise initiative, reporting initiative status and measureable outcomes to the CIOC, and for reporting changes that affect the viability and continued suitability of an initiative.
IT Enterprise Initiative: Typically a methodology, product or service shared across multiple agencies and/or staff offices.
Examples of an IT enterprise initiative are:
A common approach or set of technologies across the Department or across one or more lines of business;
An acquisition vehicle for use across the Department; or
An application or service used across the Department or across one or more lines of business.

IT enterprise initiatives in the USDA shall be managed in accordance with the guidance stated in this section and in Departmental Manual (DM) 3107-001, Management of USDA Enterprise Initiatives Procedures, as well as the USDA Enterprise IT Governance Process.
policy_statements.actor_name: IT enterprise initiatives in the USDA
cross_references: Departmental Manual (DM) 3107-001, Management of USDA Enterprise Initiatives Procedures
USDA Enterprise IT Governance Process

policy_statements.source_text: All existing IT enterprise initiatives that lack an official designation at the time this DR is published will be grandfathered by CIOC vote onto the approved IT Enterprise Initiatives Reference List.
policy_statements.resulting_status: grandfathered by CIOC vote onto the approved IT Enterprise Initiatives Reference List
conditions: that lack an official designation at the time this DR is published

policy_statements.source_text: Scope of an Enterprise Initiative:
Enterprise Scope: Whenever the CIOC designates an initiative as an enterprise initiative, it shall also designate the scope of the initiative to indicate the extent of the enterprise use intended.
conditions: Whenever the CIOC designates an initiative as an enterprise initiative

policy_statements.source_text: The following scope determinations shall be considered:

Mandatory Enterprise-wide: All organizational units of the enterprise must use the enterprise initiative for the functionality that it provides, unless an exemption is requested in writing and approved by the USDA CIO.
policy_statements.actor_name: All organizational units of the enterprise
conditions: for the functionality that it provides
unless an exemption is requested in writing and approved by the USDA CIO

policy_statements.source_text: Optional Enterprise-wide: All organizational units of the enterprise shall consider and may use the enterprise initiative for the functionality that it provides.
policy_statements.actor_name: All organizational units of the enterprise
conditions: for the functionality that it provides

policy_statements.source_text: Consistent with USDA’s Agriculture Acquisition Regulation (AGAR) Advisory No. 101, Shared First Policy in USDA Contracts, all optional enterprise-wide initiatives should be supported by a contract that is open to all USDA agencies, staff offices, and programs and provides competitive pricing for products or services.
cross_references: USDA’s Agriculture Acquisition Regulation (AGAR) Advisory No. 101, Shared First Policy in USDA Contracts

policy_statements.source_text: USDA agencies and staff offices that offer services to other USDA agencies, staff offices, and/or programs can use the CIOC’s optional enterprise-wide designation to promote the service’s value and increase enterprise awareness and use of the service.
conditions: that offer services to other USDA agencies, staff offices, and/or programs

policy_statements.source_text: Criteria for a mandatory or optional IT Enterprise Initiative:
An IT enterprise initiative must demonstrate that its use:
Meets a Common Need – the initiative must demonstrate that more than one USDA agency or staff office, or USDA as a whole, has a need for the product or service;
Is Self-Sustaining – the initiative must be able to be maintained, as an action or process, within available resources and be economical when compared to alternative solutions;
Creates Real Benefit – the initiative must demonstrate that it will achieve documented cost savings or cost avoidance for the agencies or staff offices involved; and
Offers an Effective and Efficient Approach – the initiative must demonstrate that a shared approach is better than a fragmented approach.

Enterprise Budgetary Planning: If the CIOC designates an initiative as Mandatory Enterprise-wide, it shall provide guidance to implementing organizations on the expected budgetary impact of planned costs by fiscal year.
conditions: If the CIOC designates an initiative as Mandatory Enterprise-wide

policy_statements.source_text: Whenever possible, significant expenses should be timed to begin no sooner than the budget-year-plus-one year so that programs can anticipate and plan for the cost of enterprise initiatives.

Additionally, approved initiatives should be implemented using a timeline that provides agencies and staff offices sufficient time to recoup return on existing investments and plan an orderly transition to the enterprise solution in a cost-effective manner.

Contract Preparation and Management: Program officials and/or Contracting Officer Representatives for enterprise mandatory contract vehicles shall ensure that appropriate language, such as that below, is included in acquisition requirements packages to the contracting office:
Ability for a “technology refresh” and annual review procedures (i.e., option years/periods) to ensure that the Government can take advantage when lower cost or better options become available;
policy_statements.actor_name: Program officials and/or Contracting Officer Representatives for enterprise mandatory contract vehicles

policy_statements.source_text: Exclusivity language stating that the same vendor, reseller, or manufacturer cannot renew existing contracts or create new contracts with USDA agencies and staff offices at a higher cost for the same products and services than that offered by the enterprise contract; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Program officials and/or Contracting Officer Representatives for enterprise mandatory contract vehicles

policy_statements.source_text: Additionally, for Mandatory Enterprise-wide initiatives the Department may declare a restriction for products/solutions under negotiation for an enterprise mandatory contract.
policy_statements.target: restriction for products/solutions under negotiation for an enterprise mandatory contract

policy_statements.source_text: Agencies and staff offices shall ensure that if the product/maintenance/support for that product/solution expires prior to the award of the enterprise mandatory contract vehicle, the term for the length of the renewal award is sufficient to meet agency or office mission requirements, but short enough to take advantage of the enterprise agreement as soon as practical.
conditions: if the product/maintenance/support for that product/solution expires prior to the award of the enterprise mandatory contract vehicle

policy_statements.source_text: This is required to ensure agencies and staff offices do not enter into arrangements for a product or service at a higher cost or with less favorable terms than that to be established by the enterprise initiative.
The USDA CIO shall:

Approve the acquisition and management of IT resources on behalf of any agency or staff office in the event that consensus within the CIOC cannot be reached on the initiation or continuation of a Mandatory Enterprise-wide Initiative; and
policy_statements.target: acquisition and management of IT resources
conditions: in the event that consensus within the CIOC cannot be reached on the initiation or continuation of a Mandatory Enterprise-wide Initiative

policy_statements.source_text: Override, when necessary, the CIOC’s designations regarding mandatory and optional enterprise-wide initiatives.
policy_statements.target: CIOC’s designations regarding mandatory and optional enterprise-wide initiatives

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA, OCIO, Executive Officer for Enterprise Management shall:
Maintain an IT Enterprise Initiative Reference List on a USDA corporate portal that provides a document library of all supporting artifacts related to IT Enterprise initiatives.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA, OCIO, Executive Officer for Enterprise Management

policy_statements.source_text: Provide assistance to Executive Sponsors and Initiative Owners; and
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA, OCIO, Executive Officer for Enterprise Management

policy_statements.source_text: Provide assistance with data and analysis, market research, strategic sourcing, and other technical support upon request.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA, OCIO, Executive Officer for Enterprise Management
policy_statements.target: data and analysis, market research, strategic sourcing, and other technical support

policy_statements.source_text: The CIOC shall:
Establish and oversee the process for fairly and transparently identifying, reviewing, and designating candidate initiatives as IT enterprise initiatives; and
policy_statements.target: process for fairly and transparently identifying, reviewing, and designating candidate initiatives as IT enterprise initiatives

policy_statements.source_text: Designate the Initiative Owner at the time of initiative approval.
conditions: at the time of initiative approval

policy_statements.source_text: The CIOC Advisory Board Chair shall receive form AD-3107, Request for USDA CIO Council Action, submittals for review by the CIOC Advisory Board.
cross_references: AD-3107, Request for USDA CIO Council Action

policy_statements.source_text: The CIOC Advisory Board shall:
Maintain the Request for USDA CIO Council Action Form; and
Refer complete IT enterprise initiative proposals to the CIOC.
Agency and staff office CIOs shall:
Participate actively as members of the CIOC in proposing and evaluating candidate initiatives for enterprise designation; and
Consult the IT Enterprise Initiative Reference List in advance of requesting acquisition approval for agency or staff office-specific investments.
conditions: in advance of requesting acquisition approval for agency or staff office-specific investments

policy_statements.source_text: Executive Sponsors shall be responsible for the preparation of the documentation required to support the evaluation of an enterprise initiative.
Enterprise Initiative Evaluation Working Group members shall:
Assist in the preparation of the documentation required to support the evaluation of an enterprise initiative; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Enterprise Initiative Evaluation Working Group members

policy_statements.source_text: Make recommendations to the CIOC.
policy_statements.actor_name: Enterprise Initiative Evaluation Working Group members

policy_statements.source_text: Initiative Owners shall:
Be accountable for the overall management of an approved enterprise initiative;
Report initiative status and measurable outcomes to the CIOC;
Report changes that affect the viability and continued suitability of an initiative; and
Ensure that any IT investments follow the USDA Enterprise IT Governance Process as well as all other applicable review processes.

The Office of Procurement and Property Management (OPPM) shall maintain the overall responsibility for procurement policy, advice, and coordination in acquisitions, procurement, and property management for the Department of Agriculture.
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of Procurement and Property Management (OPPM)

citation.matching_text: Management of USDA IT Enterprise Initiatives
Office of the Chief Information Officer, Enterprise Management

This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy for identifying, evaluating, and designating information technology (IT) related enterprise initiatives in the form of a recommendation to the USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO).
The intent of this DR is to promote the effective and efficient sharing of IT resources across the entire organization to drive down costs and improve customer service.
The goal is to create a structured process to address an agency’s or multiple agencies’ desire to have a shared business approach based on a single or multiple business requirements.
This DR applies to all agencies and staff offices.

Nothing in this DR is intended to supplant the delegation of authorities and responsibilities of the USDA CIO, USDA Chief Financial Officer (CFO), the Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights, and/or the Assistant Secretary for Administration under 7 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 2 or any other authorities otherwise provided by law, Federal regulation, or USDA Departmental Regulation.
The authority for this DR is derived from  7 CFR 2.89(a)(11)(x) , which authorizes the USDA CIO to improve the management and operational effectiveness of information resources.
Enterprise-wide IT initiatives present special opportunities and management challenges for USDA, given its diverse set of missions and component agencies and offices.

For example, the pooling of USDA’s purchasing power across the entire enterprise to purchase a commonly needed product can reduce the total cost of acquisition, but a shared investment in a one-dimensional service may not deliver a useful solution for all agencies and staff offices because of their mission diversity.

The CIO Council (CIOC), established by the USDA CIO and comprised of senior IT representatives from the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) and agencies and staff offices, is uniquely positioned to evaluate potential IT initiatives and designate those with the highest value as enterprise-level initiatives.

The guidance in this DR is established to ensure that IT enterprise initiatives are effectively identified, evaluated, and implemented to accomplish the best possible value for USDA agencies, staff offices, and their customers.
Executive Sponsor : The executive sponsor is a CIOC voting member from one USDA agency or staff office involved in establishing or to benefit from the enterprise initiative.
The executive sponsor shall oversee the analysis and documentation process required for the CIOC evaluation of an enterprise initiative.

Initiative Owner : The initiative owner is an official from one USDA agency or staff office involved in establishing an enterprise initiative and shall be accountable for the establishment and management of an approved enterprise initiative, reporting initiative status and measureable outcomes to the CIOC, and for reporting changes that affect the viability and continued suitability of an initiative.
IT Enterprise Initiative : Typically a methodology, product or service shared across multiple agencies and/or staff offices.
Examples of an IT enterprise initiative are:
A common approach or set of technologies across the Department or across one or more lines of business;
An acquisition vehicle for use across the Department; or
An application or service used across the Department or across one or more lines of business.

IT enterprise initiatives in the USDA shall be managed in accordance with the guidance stated in this section and in  Departmental Manual (DM) 3107-001 , *Management of USDA Enterprise Initiatives Procedures*, as well as the USDA Enterprise IT Governance Process. All existing IT enterprise initiatives that lack an official designation at the time this DR is published will be grandfathered by CIOC vote onto the approved IT Enterprise Initiatives Reference List.

Criteria for a mandatory or optional IT Enterprise Initiative:
An IT enterprise initiative must demonstrate that its use:
Meets a Common Need – the initiative must demonstrate that more than one USDA agency or staff office, or USDA as a whole, has a need for the product or service;
Is Self-Sustaining – the initiative must be able to be maintained, as an action or process, within available resources and be economical when compared to alternative solutions;
Creates Real Benefit – the initiative must demonstrate that it will achieve documented cost savings or cost avoidance for the agencies or staff offices involved; and
Offers an Effective and Efficient Approach – the initiative must demonstrate that a shared approach is better than a fragmented approach.

Enterprise Budgetary Planning**: If the CIOC designates an initiative as Mandatory Enterprise-wide, it shall provide guidance to implementing organizations on the expected budgetary impact of planned costs by fiscal year
If the CIOC designates an initiative as Mandatory Enterprise-wide
Whenever possible, significant expenses should be timed to begin no sooner than the budget-year-plus-one year so that programs can anticipate and plan for the cost of enterprise initiatives.

Additionally, approved initiatives should be implemented using a timeline that provides agencies and staff offices sufficient time to recoup return on existing investments and plan an orderly transition to the enterprise solution in a cost-effective manner.
